raw.Condition: I am unsure why DustTrak B total flow is lower than A.  They are non-flight and have been used heavily, maybe the internal filters have enough deposit to reduce the flow?
Also, the regulator was running at 12.2 to 12.35 psi during the “exhausting” time period.  We should compare that to the flight unit as well.
I revisited the last flow tests we did on 9/29/11 morning and took the average value of the A1 meter.
Here are the numbers and conditions:
1)      All tests were conducted with engineering dynamic diluter and other engineering units, not the flight units.
2)      The commanded flow to the dynamic diluter is 25 CCM for all tests
3)      The A1 meter reading units is SCCM with the standard condition being 70F (530R) and 760 torrs. The room temperature is
close to 70F. Room pressure is 742 torr . So we'll use A1 reading as CCM.
4)      The test 1 is conducted under the following conditions: dynamic diluter + TEOM + CDE-A without dustrak-A dilution. The average A1 reading is 19.7 SCCM.
5)      The test 2 is conducted under the following conditions: dynamic diluter + CDE-A + CDE-B  without dilution to either dustrak. The average A1 reading is 22.7 SCCM.
6)      The test 3 is conducted under the following conditions: dynamic diluter + TEOM + CDE-A with  dustrak-A dilution. The average A1 reading is 22.7 SCCM.
7)      From above 4) and 6), without dustrak dilution, sample flow to DD or Ptrak is 19.7 (S)CCM and with dustrak dilution, it is 22.7 (S)CCM. Again, these are based on engineering units.

8)      Some useful numbers: Ptrak flow rate is 700 CCM, Dustrak flow rate is 1700 CCM, Dustrak dilution N2 flow rate is 1000 CCM and the ionization chamber flow rate is 70 CCM. All these flow rates are fixed by critical flow orifices. TEOM flow rate is 2000 CCM fixed by its internal pump. P-trak dilution N2 flow rate varies depending on the commanded LFE rate.  Thus, with the dustrak-A (flight assignment) being replaced by TEOM, the pressure in the plumbing downstream the piston is lower than normal flight condition,
